Here's the problem. This idea only works in an equal and free market which as we know does not exist. With all the different national regulations and borders the idea that capital flight will be reduced with lower taxes is ingenuine. Every country has different tax laws and regulations (capital gains, income tax, share options, etc) and the number of legal loopholes can vary greatly from region to region.

Unfortunately economics is a pseudo-science - it is not provable with repeated experiments like physics - and because of this it is a totally subjective view seeing the Keynesian model as true or not.

In my opinion the above also means that essentially it is not down to the tax rate whether the rich pay their taxes or not, but the personal choice of the person. Students from Redondo High School disembark from the tram at the Alpine Lodge. Mount Lowe. Los Angeles. 1931 (XP from HistoricImages)

/v/HistoricImages for anyone interested.

The Mount Lowe Railway was the third in a series of scenic mountain railroads in America created as a tourist attraction on Echo Mountain and Mount Lowe, north of Los Angeles, California in the San Gabriel Mountains. The railway, existed from 1893 until its official abandonment in 1938, and had the distinction of being the only scenic mountain, electric traction (overhead electric trolley) railroad ever built in the United States.

During the seven years of operation, it constantly ran into hard times. A series of natural disasters ate away at the facilities, the first of which was a kitchen fire that destroyed the Echo Mountain House in 1900. Further fires and floods eventually destroyed any remaining facilities, and the railway was officially abandoned in 1938 after a flood washed most everything off the mountain sides.
